issues.description: Executable rewrites and removals in the migrated MM tests are not preserved in the required reasoned `Origin Rust:` blocks.
issues.rationale: The selected head rewrites constructors and fallible operations to thread tracked owners, but records them with unsupported `// Origin:` comments that give no concrete reason. It also removes runtime equality assertions from the original test without preserving them at all. The preserve-exec-code guideline in this same head requires every actual executable replacement, addition, or removal to retain a concise adjacent `Origin Rust:` block containing both the original code and the concrete reason for the change. Review comments 4560116871 and 4560116876 identify the two manifestations, and direct comparison of the exported before/after files confirms they remain in the final head.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus not executed. Independently compared the exported base and final head, checked the pinned preserve-exec-code guideline, and read all remote review threads, reviews, issue comments, and commits. The source review was AI-assisted, so it was used only as a lead and the final label was established from the fixed source evidence.

issues.description: The disabled vmspace test module adds migration rationale inside the block wrapper instead of preserving the unchanged code verbatim.
issues.rationale: The selected head inserts three explanatory lines between the opening block-comment delimiter and the original `mod vmspace` text. The same-head preserve-exec-code guideline says unchanged imports or code disabled only because it is outside the verification scope must be wrapped directly in `/* ... */`, without a reason or status narration. The review comment remains applicable to the final exported head, and the adjacent module text is otherwise the original disabled code.
